🚨 A massive financial crisis could be brewing for Anthropic.

Just days after its record breaking IPO, Wall Street is expecting Anthropic's bonds to receive a JUNK credit rating, according to WSJ.

And this comes as its stock has already crashed below its $83 IPO price.

But the bigger problem is Anthropic's MASSIVE AI spending commitments.

Here's what's happening:

• Anthropic has committed to spending $900 BILLION on AI computing power over the coming years.

• The company generated $17 BILLION in revenue last quarter, yet it's still losing money due to its enormous computing costs.

• Anthropic has $96 BILLION in cash, but its future spending commitments are nearly 10 times that amount.

• Bond investors expect its debt to receive a BB rating, below investment grade, which could make borrowing significantly more expensive.

• The entire U.S. junk bond market is worth just $1.7 TRILLION, making it difficult to raise hundreds of billions through traditional high-yield bonds.

And the implications go far beyond Anthropic.

NVIDIA and Broadcom have already guaranteed tens of billions in loans tied to AI chip purchases, while lenders are becoming increasingly concerned about the industry's massive borrowing needs.

Even established tech giants are struggling to attract bond investors, with some AI-related bonds already suffering significant losses.

Anthropic has raised enormous amounts of cash, but roughly HALF of its spending commitments stretch from 2031 all the way to 2045.

That means the company will need access to affordable financing for YEARS.

If its debt receives a junk rating, borrowing could become much more expensive, putting pressure on its AI expansion plans.

And if a company worth over $1 TRILLION struggles to finance its AI spending, the damage could spread to chipmakers, data centers and the entire AI industry.

Galatasaray are showing that reputation and Premier League price tags don't automatically make you a better football team. The intensity, confidence, organisation and hunger from Gala deserve serious credit. They're playing with the belief of a team that knows exactly what it wants, while Aston Villa are making the Premier League look far less intimidating than its fans would have us believe.

This is exactly why I keep saying the Premier League is overrated. The media hype, massive transfer fees and financial power have convinced people that English clubs are automatically superior to everyone else. Yet when they face well-organised European opposition, suddenly the so-called best league in the world starts looking very ordinary.

Credit to Galatasaray. They're not intimidated by the badge, the money or the English football hype. Maybe it's time we stopped confusing financial superiority with footballing superiority. 👏🔥
